:::{#thm-entropy-shift}
#### Shifting does not change differential entropy

Let $X$ be a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) whose [entropy](#def-entropy) exists,
and let $c$ be a real number.
Then

$$\entropyf{X + c} = \entropyf{X}.$$

[@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.6.3]

:::

::: proof

Let $Y \eqdef X + c$.
The [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $Y$ is

$$\p(Y=y) = \p(X=y-c).$$

Evaluated at $Y = X + c$, this gives

$$\p(Y=X+c) = \p(X=X).$$

Therefore

$$
\ba
\entropyf{X + c}
&= \E{-\log \p(Y=Y)} && \text{(definition of entropy)} \\
&= \E{-\log \p(Y=X+c)} && \text{(} Y = X + c \text{)} \\
&= \E{-\log \p(X=X)} && \text{(density of } Y \text{)} \\
&= \entropyf{X}. && \text{(definition of entropy)}
\ea
$$

:::
